# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Verified by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymPlayer` consumes the shared input mapping (calls `_readPlayerInput` or an extracted shared input helper) and no longer inlines the `fourDirHandler`/`asteroidsHandler` branch. Verified by a source guard and by `GymPlayer.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3** — Timed-weapon expiry, P5 multipliers and auto-fire ordering are identical in the game and every gym for the same input and `dt`. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test booting `PlayScene` and a gym, applying a P5 effect and asserting the same speed/fire-rate outcome.
- [ ] **AC4** — `GymPowerUpsCombat` no longer uses a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the player path; the player is advanced from the supplied `dt` (the enemy-clock fix is child #2).
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing scene suites pass unchanged; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard covers `_tickPlayer`.
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4.
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — new shared `_tickPlayer(dt)`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — consume the shared step.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ8 (from epic):** should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper.*

## Plan — changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0`: autoplan pre-check returned `decision: skip` (placeholder effort Extra Small / risk Low). Planning auto-completed via the six automated review stages. No child items were created: the parent epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` already decomposed register gaps 1 & 11 into this leaf task, and its ACs contain the test/verification obligations. No blocking clarifications were required; clarifications and one flagged AC wording issue are recorded below.

## Plan — automated review summary

Retained as a leaf task for direct implementation (measurable ACs + minimal implementation sketch):

- **Requirements & AC alignment:** AC1–AC7 trace to epic gaps 1 (player-control step duplicated) and 11 (`GymPlayer` not on the shared control core). AC1 names four consumers; AC2 covers `GymPlayer`; AC4 covers `GymPowerUpsCombat`; together they cover every consumer named in the summary. OQ8 is answered by AC2.
- **Completeness:** `## Acceptance Criteria` is present and the `## Key Files` paths are syntactically valid; all 11 referenced files exist at HEAD (`7bfe98f`).
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children. This item is the prerequisite (epic child #1) for boss integration (child #6) and the parity guard (child #10). Tests are embedded in AC1–AC5, so the test-first intent is satisfied without separate children.
- **Scope sizing:** one focused refactor (add `_tickPlayer`, migrate six scenes, tests, docs) — a deliverable increment.
- **Acceptance & testability:** all ACs are pass/fail; AC3 (cross-scene equivalence) and AC5 (duplicate-body guard) name automated verification.
- **Polish & handoff:** description is actionable; the Key Files list matches the consumer set.
- **AC coverage review:** `run_coverage_review` returned `recommendation: proceed` (leaf item; no children).

## Plan — clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: "OQ8 — should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal?" Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Research (HEAD `7bfe98f`; read of `PlayScene.tick` L557–572, `GymFormationScene.tick` L1299–1318, `GymWeapons.tick` L178–195, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` L154–170, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick` L258–275): the scenes run **subsets with different ordering**, not identical copies — `PlayScene` runs tickWeaponTimers → multipliers → `_handleTeleport` → input → physics → auto-fire; `GymFormationScene` runs timers → multipliers → input → physics → auto-fire with teleport later; `GymWeapons` omits the P5 multipliers; `GymPowerUpsUtility` omits tickWeaponTimers and auto-fire; `GymPowerUpsCombat` omits timers, multipliers and auto-fire. Resolution (epic assumption, "the shipped game is canonical"): the shared `_tickPlayer(dt)` runs the full ordered sequence and each gym's absent feature resolves to a no-op (multiplier 1, empty weapon list). Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" Research: the only fixed 16 ms step is `_nextFireTime += 16` inside `_tickScouts` (`GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` L424), which is the **enemy-fire** clock and belongs to epic child #2 (`AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46`, "Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock"); the player path already advances from the supplied `dt`. **OPEN QUESTION (AC4 wording):** AC4 should be read as "the `GymPowerUpsCombat` player path uses the supplied `dt`" (already true); the 16 ms enemy clock is fixed by child #2, not by this item. Intent is clear enough to implement; the wording is flagged for correction rather than rewritten here (rewriting could change intent).

**OQ-NOTE (effort/risk):** the autoplan pre-check generated a zeroed placeholder estimate (O=M=P=0, 0.00 h → Extra Small / Low) because `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` submits a fixed `{o:0,m:0,p:0}` payload. Treat the `effort`/`risk` fields as a placeholder; `<WIP-id>` should receive a genuine `/skill:effort-and-risk` estimate before implementation is dispatched.

# Intake Brief — Add a mineral scoop power-up (AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ)

**Headline:** Add a **P10 Mineral Scoop** power-up that attracts nearby minerals toward the ship, mirroring the P9 Magnet's ergonomics for the mineral field: timed (15 s, refresh-only) as a field pickup and permanent-stacking (cap 5) as a hold-full upgrade, implemented once in shared code so the game and both relevant gyms run identical behaviour.

## Problem statement

Minerals are the only collectable in the game with no attraction assist: they are stationary and must be flown over one at a time, which is laborious on mineral-dense fields (e.g. after an asteroid chain or an enemy re-drop). The **P9 Magnet** already solves the identical ergonomics problem for power-up/weapon drops. A **P10 Mineral Scoop** power-up gives the player the parallel, mineral-targeted convenience — an attraction field whose target entity set is the mineral field rather than the drop list.

## Users

- **Player** — wants to sweep up scattered minerals without having to steer precisely onto each gold dot.
- **Developer** — wants the attraction implemented once in shared code so `PlayScene` and every relevant gym run the same behaviour (repo-wide gym↔game parity rule).

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a **P10 Mineral Scoop** field drop, nearby minerals drift toward my ship for a while so I can fill my hold faster.
- As a player, when I choose P10 as a **hold-full reward**, the mineral attraction becomes a permanent part of my run, so I never lose the convenience.
- As a developer, the scoop attraction is defined once and consumed by `PlayScene` and both the mineral and utility gyms, so it cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **New power-up P10 exists and is spawnable.** `P10` is added to `PowerUpId`, `PowerUpType` (`MINERAL_SCOOP`) and `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` with a player-facing name and one-line description; it is included in the weighted drop spawn pool (`POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` / default standard weight) and in the hold-full choice pool (`CHOICE_POOL`). Verified by catalogue/spawner/choice unit tests.
- [ ] **Field pickup is a timed, refreshing effect.** Collecting P10 as a field drop activates a **15 s** mineral-attraction effect; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full and does **not** add permanent stacks. Verified by `src/powerups/effects` unit tests (activation, expiry after 15 s, refresh, no permanent stack).
- [ ] **Hold-full upgrade is a permanent stacking effect.** Applying P10 as a permanent reward (`applyCollect('P10', true)`, i.e. the `applyMineralChoiceReward` path) grants a permanent attraction that stacks up to **5**, with radius `2 × ship size × (1 + 0.5 × stacks)` and pull speed `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED` (120 px/s). Verified by effects unit tests (permanent, stacking, cap).
- [ ] **Shared attraction helper, one implementation.** A single exported helper (e.g. `applyMineralScoop` / `applyMineralAttraction`) pulls live, collectible minerals within the scoop radius toward the player at `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED` and syncs each mineral's rendered position. It is called from every scene that owns a mineral field (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`). Verified by unit tests for the helper (in-range pull, out-of-range no-op, no-op with zero effect) and by the repo-wide duplicate-body/equivalence parity guard.
- [ ] **Enabled in the game and both gyms (parity).** P10 is exercised in `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals` (existing mineral field) and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (a mineral field is added there so the enabled behaviour runs the same shared code). The gym help overlay lists P10 with its icon and the catalogue description. Verified by scene tests for each and the parity/help tests.
- [ ] **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, the GDD §4.4 power-up table/notes, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Parity rule (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once in `src/scenes/core/` / `src/powerups/` and is consumed by both the game and the gyms; no divergent copy. The duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs assertion must stay green. Only a *disabled* feature may differ; an enabled scoop must run the same code everywhere.
- **Tuning decisions (operator, this intake):** duration **15 s**; radius/stacking parameters **same as P9 Magnet** (base 2× ship size, +50%/stack, cap 5, 120 px/s); timed pickups **refresh only, no stack**; id **P10**.
- **Timed vs permanent:** the timed (field) and permanent (upgrade) states must both be represented; the timed state must expire on the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick`.
- **Paused when phased?** Mineral collection is gated by P6 Phase Shift (`collectMinerals({ playerPhased })`). The scoop should attract minerals on the same terms as collection — i.e. it does not grant collection while phased, and (consistent with the existing magnet) attraction itself may still run; the brief treats the collection gate as unchanged. Implementation must keep the phased gate behaviour identical to today.
- No new activation key; the scoop is passive like the magnet.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (ship skill owns it).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) already models timed effects (`SHIELD`, `SPEED_BOOST`) with refresh-not-additive semantics and permanent stack state (`_magnetStacks`, cap `P9_MAX_STACKS`). `applyCollect(id, permanent)` already carries the "upgrade" flag used by `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- `src/powerups/magnet.ts` has the shared drop-attraction helper `applyMagnetAttraction(drops, player, stacks, dt)` operating on a structural `MovableDrop` (x/y + `graphics.setPosition` + `powerUp.canCollect()`).
- Minerals (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`) are `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` with public `x`/`y`, `alive`, and `handleOverlap`; they are stationary (`updatePosition` is a no-op). Collection/absorption is the shared `collectMinerals` (`src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`).
- Mineral fields live in `PlayScene` (`_handleMinerals`) and `GymFormationScene` (`_updateMinerals`), inherited by `GymMinerals`; `GymPowerUpsUtility` has **no** mineral field today.
- Drop spawner pool is `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` (`src/core/rules.ts`); the hold-full choice pool is `CHOICE_POOL` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`); help rows come from `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` via `src/utils/gymHelp.ts`; icons are code-drawn in `src/powerups/icons.ts`; pickup cues dispatch in `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`.
- The GDD §4.4 table documents P3–P9, with the Magnet described as permanent. It has no mineral-attraction entry.

## Desired change

Add **P10 Mineral Scoop**, a magnet-analogue whose target is the mineral field:

- **Field drop:** timed 15 s attraction, refreshes on re-collection (no stacking).
- **Hold-full upgrade:** permanent, stacking (cap 5) attraction.
- A shared attraction helper (`src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts`) mirroring `magnet.ts`, called from the game and gyms before mineral collection.
- Catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool, icon, help, HUD display, and docs updated; the utility gym gains a mineral field so the scoop is demonstrable there.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `P10` to `PowerUpId`, `PowerUpType.MINERAL_SCOOP`, and `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (name + description).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — timed P10 state + permanent stacking state; `scoopStacks()` / scoop accessors; include P10 in `activeEffects()`; reset in `reset()`.
- `src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts` *(new)* — shared `applyMineralScoop` attraction helper + scoop radius function (mirrors `magnet.ts` / `magnetRadius`).
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — optionally host/expose the scoop pass alongside `collectMinerals`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — apply scoop attraction before `_handleMinerals` collection.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — apply scoop attraction before `_updateMinerals` (inherited by `GymMinerals`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — add a mineral field, spawn P10, apply scoop attraction.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — add `'P10'` to `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` and the standard weight.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add `'P10'` to `CHOICE_POOL`.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — P10 colour + code-drawn scoop icon.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — pickup cue (reuse the magnet cue unless a dedicated one is added).
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — pickup-cue dispatch for P10; drop-id enumerations in tests.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — timed/stack display for P10 (likely generic already).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 table + notes for P10; README power-up list.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, new `src/powerups/mineralScoop.test.ts`, `src/powerups/magnet.test.ts` / parity guards, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`, `src/utils/gymHelp.test.ts`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the timed/permanent split maps cleanly onto the existing `applyCollect(id, permanent)` flag, which already drives the hold-full reward path. *Mitigation:* add registry unit tests for both paths before scene wiring.
- **Risk — HUD rendering for a dual timed/stacked type.** The HUD already renders timed countdowns and stack counts, but P10 changes type between pickups and upgrades; the display must not show a misleading `×0`. *Mitigation:* only surface stacks/remaining when active, mirroring the existing P6 zero-charge rule.
- **Risk — parity drift.** Gyms could diverge if the scoop pass is inlined per scene. *Mitigation:* the duplicate-body/equivalence guard plus a dedicated helper unit test; call the shared helper from every scene.
- **Risk — GymPowerUpsUtility has no mineral field.** Adding one changes a threat-free gym's contents and existing tests. *Mitigation:* scope the field to the gym, update its tests, and keep minerals inert to enemies there (no enemies exist).
- **Assumption:** reusing the generic/Magnet pickup cue is acceptable; a dedicated scoop cue is optional polish, not required by an AC.
- **Assumption:** phased players may still have minerals attracted (the collection gate is unchanged), matching the existing magnet's relationship to collection.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the P9 Magnet consistency change (AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L) and any generic "attractor target predicate" refactor are **out of scope** here and tracked as separate work items; the scoop is a parallel helper, not a rewrite of `magnet.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUJRVZP2002G8GC — Shared mineral-seek seam parity** (completed): established the shared mineral-field seam consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`; the scoop plugs into the same mineral-field access `setSeekTargets`-style seam.

Planned 2026-10-04. Decomposed into **10 children** — 4 test-first tasks, 5 implementation features, 1 docs/validation task — with 17 dependency edges. Test-first ordering follows the established `effects.permanent.test.ts` convention: the test tasks land first (initially red) and the feature tasks make them green. ## Summary

Add the single shared implementation that pulls minerals toward the ship,
mirroring `magnet.ts` so the game and every gym run the same code. Covers parent
AC4 of AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New `src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts` exports a single `applyMineralScoop(minerals, player, stacks, dt)` helper that pulls live (`alive`) minerals within the scoop radius toward the player at `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED` and syncs each mineral's rendered position.
- A `scoopRadius(shipSize, stacks)` function returns `2 × shipSize × (1 + 0.5 × stacks)`, sharing the magnet tuning constants (no divergent copy of the formula).
- The helper is a no-op for zero effective stacks or out-of-range minerals and never collects, hides or destroys a mineral (collection remains `collectMinerals`).
- `CombatCoreScene` exposes a shared `_applyMineralScoop(minerals, dt)` template method that calls the helper with the registry's effective scoop stacks.
- The tests from "Test: Shared mineral scoop attraction helper semantics" are green and the pre-existing suite still passes.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts` mirroring `magnet.ts`, with a structural `MovableMineral` interface (`x`, `y`, `alive`, `setPosition`).
2. Factor the shared attraction-radius formula so `magnetRadius` and `scoopRadius` delegate to one implementation (or share the same constants) — no duplicated body.
3. Add the `_applyMineralScoop` template method to `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, reading `getEffectsRegistry().scoopEffectStacks()`.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts` (new)
- `src/powerups/effects.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/powerups/mineralScoop.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- P10 effects — timed pickup and permanent stacking (the registry effective-stack accessor).
- Test: Shared mineral scoop attraction helper semantics (prerequisite).

## Deliverables

One shared scoop attraction implementation, unit-tested.

# Mineral field and P10 in GymPowerUpsUtility

## Summary

Make the threat-free utility gym demonstrate P10: give it a live mineral field,
spawn P10 in its round-robin, run the shared scoop pass, and list P10 in its help
overlay. Covers the utility-gym half of parent AC5 of AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GymPowerUpsUtility` owns a live mineral field (seeded on create and reseeded so a demonstration field is always present), destroyed on teardown.
- The gym runs the same shared scoop pass and collects minerals via the shared `collectMinerals` (no enemies absorb them there).
- P10 is added to the gym's round-robin spawn order and its help drop list, so the help overlay lists P10 with its icon and catalogue description.
- The utility-gym/help cases from "Test: P10 parity across PlayScene, GymMinerals and GymPowerUpsUtility" are green and the pre-existing gym/help tests still pass.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add a `minerals: Mineral[]` field to `GymPowerUpsUtility`, seeded via `scatterMineralDrops` (reseed when depleted) and destroyed in `teardownRunState`.
2. Add `'P10'` to `NON_COMBAT_ORDER` and the `addHelpButton` drops list.
3. Call `this._applyMineralScoop(this.minerals, dt)` then `this.minerals = collectMinerals(this.minerals, this.player, [], () => {})` in `tick`.
